items.prompt: What is 'validation,' as this unit defines it?
choices: Cheaply testing whether an assumption about what people want is actually true, before spending the effort to build the full solution
A formal legal review that a product must pass before it's allowed to launch publicly
Getting explicit sign-off from a manager before the team starts work on a project
Running a full suite of automated tests against a feature's underlying source code
items.explanation: Validation is specifically about cheaply testing an assumption before committing full build effort — not a legal, managerial, or automated-testing process.
items.reference:
Validation
💰 Cheap test
🎯 Of an assumption, before full build effort
Why: the point is confirming direction before spending the expensive effort.

items.prompt: In L1, what step did the team skip before building the six-week export feature?
choices: Validation of the underlying assumption that customers wanted a raw data export
A thorough code review of the finished export feature before it went out the door
A dedicated meeting with the sales team to discuss the original request in more depth
Writing complete documentation explaining how to use the new export feature
items.explanation: The team built directly from an assumption relayed by sales, without any cheap test to confirm what customers actually wanted before committing six weeks of engineering.
items.reference:
Validation
💰 Cheap test
🎯 Of an assumption, before full build effort
Why: the point is confirming direction before spending the expensive effort.

items.prompt: What is a 'prototype,' as this unit defines it?

The final, fully polished version of a feature that's considered ready for public release
A detailed technical specification document written before any code gets written
A backup copy of a feature's existing source code kept in case something breaks
items.explanation: A prototype exists to answer a question cheaply — it's explicitly not meant to be the shipped, production version of the feature.
items.reference:
Prototype
⚡ Fast, low effort
❓ Built to test a question
Why: a prototype's job is answering a question, not being shippable.

items.prompt: What does this unit say an MVP (minimum viable product) actually is?
choices: The smallest version of an idea that can test the riskiest assumption behind it
The cheapest possible version of the final feature that still technically works
A product with the fewest possible bugs at launch
The first version of a product released to the public
items.explanation: L1 explicitly distinguishes an MVP from 'a smaller, cheaper version of the final feature' — its defining job is testing the riskiest assumption, not being a reduced version of the eventual product.
items.reference:
MVP
🎯 Tests the riskiest assumption
🚫 Not just 'smaller final feature'
Why: this distinction is the most common misreading of the term.

MVP

Assumption vs. evidence
💭 Assumption: unconfirmed belief
👁️ Evidence: real behavioral signal
Why: validation exists specifically to convert one into the other.
